headline_marked: 10 tourists killed as [[Cox’s Bazar resort gutted by fire]]
headline: 10 tourists killed as Cox’s Bazar resort gutted by fire
summary: A Dhaka University student and five of his family members are among the dead. The resort had been flagged as hazardous and lacked a fire safety licence.
details: Ten tourists were killed in a devastating fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort near Inani Beach in Cox’s Bazar's Ukhiya this morning.

The victims include Md Nafis Tehami, a student of Chinese language and culture at Dhaka University, and five of his family members: Mithila Mehjabin Alvi, Laila Jahan Nabila, Maliha Mila, Sabrin, and child Faizan Ahmed.
A total of nine family members were staying at the resort; six died and three were injured. The dead included four female cousins, one male cousin, and a child.
The three injured family members are currently receiving treatment at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital.
The Fire Service and Civil Defence (FSCD) revealed that the resort was operating without a fire safety licence.
According to the FSCD, an inspector had visited the resort in June and served a formal notice on June 11, flagging the structure as hazardous.
DU Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam expressed deep sorrow and called for the cause of the fire to be identified and those responsible brought to justice.
caption:
10 tourists killed in a Cox's Bazar resort fire. A DU student and five of his family members are among the dead.

Ten tourists were killed in a devastating fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort near Inani Beach in Cox’s Bazar's Ukhiya this morning.

The victims include Md Nafis Tehami, a student of Chinese language and culture at Dhaka University, and five of his family members: Mithila Mehjabin Alvi, Laila Jahan Nabila, Maliha Mila, Sabrin, and child Faizan Ahmed.

A total of nine family members were staying at the resort; six died and three were injured. The dead included four female cousins, one male cousin, and a child.

The three injured family members are currently receiving treatment at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital.

The Fire Service and Civil Defence (FSCD) revealed that the resort was operating without a fire safety licence.

According to the FSCD, an inspector had visited the resort in June and served a formal notice on June 11, flagging the structure as hazardous.

DU Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam expressed deep sorrow and called for the cause of the fire to be identified and those responsible brought to justice.

headline_marked: 6 units of Fire Service [[fire at Ibn Sina pharmaceutical factory]] brought under control
headline: 6 units of Fire Service fire at Ibn Sina pharmaceutical factory brought under control
summary: The blaze broke out in the herbal section of the factory in Gazipur's Kaliakair upazila on Saturday afternoon.
details: A fire erupted at the Ibn Sina Pharmaceuticals factory in the Safipur area of Kaliakair upazila, Gazipur, on Saturday afternoon.
The blaze started around 4:30 PM and was brought under control by 5:35 PM through the efforts of six units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence.
According to reports, the fire originated in the herbal section of the factory and spread rapidly.
Initially, three units of the Fire Service arrived at the scene to combat the blaze, later joined by additional units.
No immediate reports of casualties or the cause of the fire have been released.
This incident follows another fire at the Drug International factory in Tongi, Gazipur, last Wednesday, which took approximately four hours to control.
caption:
A pharmaceutical factory in Gazipur was engulfed in flames on Saturday afternoon.

A fire erupted at the Ibn Sina Pharmaceuticals factory in the Safipur area of Kaliakair upazila, Gazipur, on Saturday afternoon.

The blaze started around 4:30 PM and was brought under control by 5:35 PM through the efforts of six units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence.

According to reports, the fire originated in the herbal section of the factory and spread rapidly.

Initially, three units of the Fire Service arrived at the scene to combat the blaze, later joined by additional units.

No immediate reports of casualties or the cause of the fire have been released.

This incident follows another fire at the Drug International factory in Tongi, Gazipur, last Wednesday, which took approximately four hours to control.
